entities.summary: George Tucker was an American author, educator and historian in Virginia, following early years as an attorney and politician. His literary works include The Valley of Shenandoah (1824), the first fiction of colonial life in Virginia, and A Voyage to the Moon (1827), which is among the nation's earliest science fiction novels. He also published the first comprehensive biography of Thomas Jefferson in 1837, as well as his History of the United States (1856). Tucker's authorship, and his work as a teacher, served to redeem an earlier life of unprincipled habits which had brought him some disrepute.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Tucker's literary works, particularly A Voyage to the Moon and The Valley of Shenandoah, contributed to the development of American literature. His comprehensive biography of Thomas Jefferson helped shape public perception of the founding father.
